The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.6,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road Shri Kumar T.N vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102605033/

sentences.text: The brief facts of the petition are as under:

On 18.1.2018 at about 9.00 p.m. the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-52-L-7220 on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-4 service road from his place towards Nelamangala, when he reached near Ravathanahalli gate, a car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495 driven by its driver came from Dasanapura side towards Ravuthanahalli gate side in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to VP Magnus Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 52 years, Security Guard and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement and the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and placed exparte.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.
KA-32-M- 5495 and its validity.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.
134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-02-ML-5974 on 20.4.2018 at about 8.00 p.m. near Haralur gate, on Hosakote-Malur Road, Hosakote?

7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P18.
8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P5 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
15. On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by one Kumara, Son of Nanjaiah on 19.1.2018.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Nelamangala Traffic Police in Cr.No.31/2018 against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
On perusal of Ex.P2 is spot mahazar also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborate the evidence of PW1.
Ex.P3 is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to both the vehicles and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex.P4 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed Shri Kumar T.N vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102605033/
3 charge sheet against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.

sentences.text: The counsel for the respondent No.1 has argued that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the car.
To substantiate the said fact, the respondent has not examined any witness on its behalf.
On the other hand petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 18.1.2018 at about 9.00 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to VP Magnus Hospital,
Nelamangala, wherein he took the treatment as inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P4, which discloses the following injuries;
1)Abrasion wound over both lower limb 2)Dislocation of left shoulder 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 18.1.2018 to 20.1.2018 and relocation of the dislocated shoulder.
21. PW2- Dr.Manjunath has produced the documents marked at Ex.P14 to Ex.P18 such as authorization letter, MLC extract, police intimation, case sheet and X-rays.

22. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
23. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 52 years, security guard and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
He has produced Aadhar card, employment card and statement of account which are marked at Ex.P7, Ex.P8 and Ex.P9.
Though he has produced the statement of account, which does not disclose the exact amount of his salary.
In the absence of the documents pertains to his income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.

So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner, if notional income of Rs.8,000/- per month is considered, it will meet Shri Kumar T.N vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102605033/
4 the ends of justice.

sentences.text: the petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which shows that he was admitted from 18.1.2018 to 20.1.2018.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries; he might have taken rest and treatment at least for one month.
Therefore, one month income comes to Rs.8,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
24. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.27,872/- and advance receipt marked at Ex.P11 and prescriptions marked at Ex.P12.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.27,872/- towards medical expenses.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 52 years, working as a security guard and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he is getting pain in his shoulder, not able to sleep on his left side and not able to lift weight with his left hand and not able to drive/or ride any vehicle.
the petitioner has produced x-ray marked at Ex.P13.
The petitioner has not examine the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability.
Therefore, no amount is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of future earning.
26. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, so his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.
Further he took the treatment as inpatient.

On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 18.1.2018 to 20.1.2018 and also took the treatment as outpatient.
So, one must attend him during the above said period.

Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc..
27.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs. 25,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 8,000-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 27,872-00 4. Loss of future income Nil 5. Loss of amenities, Attendant, Rs. 15,000-00 Nourishment and conveyance charges

sentences.text: LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495.
29.
The respondent No.1 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
30. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,872/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 2nd day of April 2019).
(MAHANTESH S.DARGAD) III ADDL.SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & XXIX ACMM, BANGALORE.
